sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Rudyard Kipling is popularly believed to have written part of 'Kim' in Bundi and famously described Bundi Palace as 'the work of goblins rather than of men.' Ruled by the Hada Chauhans; once considered capital of the Hadoti Kingdom, known for art and sculpture; Kota separated as an independent state in 1624, beginning Bundi's decline. Architecture carries a bluish hue (like Jodhpur) to keep houses cool.

places.name: Sukh Mahal
places.facts: Small two-storied summer-retreat palace; famous as the place where Kipling reportedly wrote 'Kim'; part of a film adaptation was shot here.

places.name: Kshar Bag (Saar Bagh)
places.location: Near Chhatra Vilas Garden, Shikar Burj Jait Sagar Road
places.facts: Houses the memorial cenotaphs of the Bundi royal family.

places.name: Raniji Ki Baori
places.facts: 'Queen's Stepwell', built 1699 by Rani Nathavati Ji, younger queen of Rao Raja Anirudh Singh; multi-storied; carvings of Gajraj (elephant) with trunk turned inward as if drinking from the baori; high arched gate.

places.name: Dabhai Kund
places.facts: Also called Jail Kund; largest stepwell of its kind in Bundi, shaped like an inverted pyramid; fantastic carvings on the steps leading to the water.

places.name: Nagar Sagar Kund
places.facts: Twin stepwells built to provide water during famine.

places.name: Taragarh Fort, Bundi
places.facts: Built 1354; ramshackle, overgrown with vegetation but pleasant for a stroll; curved roofs, pavilions, temple columns, elephant and lotus motifs in Rajput style.

places.name: 84 Pillared Cenotaph
places.facts: Structure supported by 84 columns; commissioned by Rao Anirudh, Maharaja of Bundi, as a tribute to his wet nurse Deva; carvings of deer, elephants, apsaras.

places.name: Lake Jait Sagar
places.facts: Scenic lake surrounded by hills; lotus flowers bloom in winter and monsoon.

places.name: Lake Nawal Sagar
places.facts: Artificial lake visible from Taragarh Fort; half-submerged temple to Lord Varun Dev at its centre; reflects nearby palaces and forts.

places.name: Lake Kanak Sagar, Dugari
places.facts: Flat lake with an eponymous town; migratory birds year-round including bar-headed goose and Demoiselle cranes.

places.name: Ramgarh Vishdhari Wildlife Sanctuary (Ramgarh Tiger Reserve)
places.facts: 252 sq km; established 1982; forms a buffer for Ranthambore National Park; best visited September-May.

places.name: Phool Sagar
places.facts: Private royal-family property; artificial lake named for the palace on its banks; palace houses paintings by Italian prisoners; special permission required to visit.

places.name: Garh Palace, Bundi
places.facts: Among the largest palaces in India; built by different rulers over ~3 centuries; Rajput architecture with elephant-carved jharokhas and pillars; includes Chhatra Mahal, Phool Mahal, Badal Mahal, and the Chitrashala miniature-mural gallery. Open 8am-5pm; small entry fee; guides available.

places.name: Badal Mahal
places.facts: 'Palace of Clouds'; walls covered in paintings showing early Chinese cultural influence; verandah/ground floor built by Maharawal Gopinath, rest built 1609-1657 by Maharawal Punjraj; made of Dawra stone; arches feature half-ready lotus motifs, the longest vault has three.

places.name: Hathi Pole
places.facts: The more popular of two main Garh Palace entrance gates; features two bugle-blowing elephant carvings; commissioned by Rao Ratan Singh.

places.name: Chhatra Mahal
places.facts: Once a garden palace with fountains and fish pools; 'Chhatr' relates to its painted murals; site of the innermost Chitrashala chamber (painting house) commissioned by king Umed Singh; miniature paintings of gods, battle scenes, Radha-Krishna, preserved by lack of sunlight/moisture exposure.

places.name: Shikar Burj
places.location: Near Sarbagh, a little distance from Sukh Mahal, Bundi
places.facts: Old royal hunting cottage; retreat of Umed Singh, 18th-century ruler of Bundi, after renouncing the throne; now a popular picnic spot.

places.name: Bhimlat Waterfall
places.facts: Popular picnic spot with an old Shiva temple and a 140-foot-high waterfall.

howToReach.air: Nearest airport is Sanganer Airport, Jaipur, ~206 km away
howToReach.rail: Railway station ~4 km south of the old city; rail connections between Bundi and Chittorgarh
howToReach.road: Regular buses from Ajmer, Bijolia, Bikaner, Chittorgarh, Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, and Udaipur
